record.paper_title: Basic Properties of Strong Mixing Conditions. A Survey and Some Open Questions
record.original_question: Let B be an arbitrary nontrivial real Banach space with dual space B*. For two sigma-fields A and B0, define R^{B}_{∞,∞}(A,B0) as the supremum of |E⟨X,Y⟩ - ⟨EX,EY⟩| divided by || ||X||_B ||_∞ · || ||Y||_{B*} ||_∞, where the supremum ranges over simple B-valued random variables X that are A-measurable and simple B*-valued random variables Y that are B0-measurable. Must this dependence measure always be equivalent, in the sense of becoming arbitrarily small exactly when the other does, to either the alpha-dependence coefficient or the beta-dependence coefficient?

evidence.quote: Following (essentially) the notations in [47], for any two σ-fields A and B, define the measure of dependence R_B^{∞,∞}(A, B) := sup |E⟨X, Y ⟩ − ⟨EX, EY ⟩| / (|| ||X||_B ||_∞ · || ||Y ||_{B∗} ||_∞).
Question 1: For an arbitrary nontrivial real Banach space B, is the measure of dependence R_B^{∞,∞}(·, ·) equivalent to one of the two measures of dependence α(·, ·), β(·, ·)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B$ be an arbitrary nontrivial real Banach space with continuous dual $B^*$, and let $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\colon B\times B^*\to\mathbb{R}$ denote the canonical duality pairing. Fix a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$. For any two sub-$\sigma$-fields $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{F}$, define
$$R^{B}_{\infty,\infty}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) \;:=\; \sup\frac{\bigl|E\langle X,Y\rangle - \langle EX,EY\rangle\bigr|}{\bigl\|\,\|X\|_B\,\bigr\|_\infty\;\bigl\|\,\|Y\|_{B^*}\,\bigr\|_\infty},$$
where the supremum is taken over all simple $B$-valued random variables $X$ that are $\mathcal{A}$-measurable and all simple $B^*$-valued random variables $Y$ that are $\mathcal{B}$-measurable (with the convention $0/0=0$).

Recall the classical real-valued dependence coefficients
$$\alpha(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) := \sup_{A\in\mathcal{A},\,B\in\mathcal{B}}|P(A\cap B)-P(A)P(B)|,$$
$$\beta(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) := \tfrac{1}{2}\sup\sum_{i,j}|P(A_i\cap B_j)-P(A_i)P(B_j)|,$$
where the second supremum is over all finite measurable partitions $\{A_i\}\subset\mathcal{A}$ and $\{B_j\}\subset\mathcal{B}$.

Say that two families of dependence measures $D_1,D_2$ are equivalent if, uniformly over choices of probability space and pair of $\sigma$-fields, $D_1(\mathcal{A}_n,\mathcal{B}_n)\to 0$ if and only if $D_2(\mathcal{A}_n,\mathcal{B}_n)\to 0$.

Question: Is it true that for every nontrivial real Banach space $B$, the dependence measure $R^{B}_{\infty,\infty}(\cdot,\cdot)$ is equivalent (in the sense above) to either $\alpha(\cdot,\cdot)$ or $\beta(\cdot,\cdot)$?
artifact.category_tag: Strong mixing conditions for Banach-valued random variables
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open question in R. C. Bradley's 2005 survey on basic properties of strong mixing conditions. A search of subsequent literature (including Bradley's later work on dependence coefficients for Banach-valued random variables and surveys/reviews citing the 2005 survey) did not turn up a published resolution either confirming or refuting the equivalence; the problem appears to still be open.
